card.summary: 'Self-hosted ingress proxy & VPN tunnel. Securely exposes private local & Docker-based services to the Internet, with free, automatically renewable SSL certi...

free_tier.stated: 'Self-hosted ingress proxy & VPN tunnel. Securely exposes private local & Docker-based services to the Internet, with free, automatically renewable SSL certificates.' MIT licensed; no vendor quota.

egress.terms: No allowance is published; the gateway host's own egress is the limit.; ingress: tcp+udp

record.chaining: the same free-tier VPS shape as Pangolin and Wiredoor: one host, one WireGuard mesh, public ports bound on the host

limits.value: the software imposes no byte meter; what runs out is the monthly allowance of the host it runs on, and that host is a separate provider

record.binding_note: the software imposes no byte meter; what runs out is the monthly allowance of the host it runs on, and that host is a separate provider

identity_cost.detail: Self-hosted open-source software: no vendor account at all.

record.reliability_note: the gateway is a single public Linux host; losing it loses every published service
record.confidence_note: A published UDP service through a real gateway would raise this to measured.

evidence.proved: 'Reverse proxy with support for HTTP(S) 1/2/3, WebSocket, gRPC (over HTTP/2) and TCP/UDP (Layer-4)'; 'Powered by WireGuard, CoreDNS and Caddy'

the gateway is 'a Linux-based machine with Docker installed, a public IP address, and the following open ports: 80/tcp, 443/tcp, 4060/tcp, 51820/udp and 32420-32421/tcp+udp', via the search index snippet of the README

record.notes: Found by the required search 'wireguard ingress public', not on the supplied list. The README body carries the L4 TCP/UDP claim; the gateway port list came from the search index snippet, so that row is one rung weaker than the rest.

extras.wg_detail: 'Powered by WireGuard, CoreDNS and Caddy'. The CLI or Docker labels drive the tunnel; no .conf export is documented.
extras.volume_stated: No allowance is published; the gateway host's own egress is the limit.
extras.transit_note: the gateway terminates and relays; the bytes cross its public NIC both ways
